summary: IDS feed s092_single is degraded: 4.2% of frames (113/2711) exceed the IDS 1G port MTU (1518 bytes) and are dropped by the NIC, creating a detection blind spot. No other visibility faults detected.

findings.root_cause: Network is carrying jumbo frames (up to 8058 bytes, consistent with 9000-byte MTU on switches/servers) while the IDS 1 Gbps capture port is set to standard 1518-byte MTU. The packet broker is forwarding frames unchanged, so the IDS NIC drops any frame >1518 bytes.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently drops 4.2% of frames before inspection. Because this IDS needs full payload for signature matching, those flows are invisible, reducing detection coverage and allowing attacks hidden in large frames to be missed.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs full payload so slicing/trimming to 1518 bytes is not an option (would break IDS inspection). Must enable jumbo frame support on the IDS capture port and packet-broker egress to 9000-9216 bytes, or normalize MTU upstream, so large frames are delivered intact without NIC drops.
